text: Databases store and organise information so we can find it quickly. There are two main types: SQL and NoSQL. SQL databases use tables with rows and columns, like a spreadsheet. NoSQL databases are more flexible and store data in other forms, such as documents. To get information, we write queries — special commands that ask the database questions. Data modeling means planning how to structure the data before we build the database. Finally, indexes help the database find data faster, just like an index in a book. Choosing the right type and design makes applications work better.
